topics.title: Design a Unique ID Generator
topics.description: Understanding distributed ID generation approaches including UUID, ticket servers, and Snowflake-style algorithms.

subtopics.title: Problem Definition
subtopics.theory:
1️⃣ Problem Definition

✅ Definition

Unique ID Generator in Distributed Systems is a mechanism that generates globally unique, time-sortable IDs across multiple machines without collisions.



✅ Important Requirements

Uniqueness

Time-ordering (sortable)

64-bit constraint

Numeric only

High throughput

Low latency

Distributed scalability

subtopics.title: Auto-Increment ID
subtopics.theory:
🔹 A) Auto-Increment ID

Definition

Database feature where ID increases automatically by 1 for each new record.

Flow

Insert row

DB increments counter

Returns next ID

Advantages

Very simple

Naturally ordered

Disadvantages

Not distributed

Single point of failure

Scaling issues

subtopics.title: Multi-Master Auto-Increment
subtopics.theory:
🔹 B) Multi-Master Auto-Increment

Definition

Multiple DB servers generate IDs using offset + step logic.

Flow

Each server assigned offset

Increment by number of servers

Generate ID independently

Advantages

No central coordinator

Rough ordering

Disadvantages

Hard to add/remove servers

Rebalancing is complex

Wastes ID space

subtopics.title: UUID
subtopics.theory:
🔹 C) UUID (Universally Unique Identifier)

Definition

128-bit random-based globally unique identifier.

Flow

Generate random/hash-based 128-bit number

Assign as ID

Advantages

No coordination

Extremely low collision probability

Simple to implement

Disadvantages

Not time sortable

Large size (128-bit)

Poor DB index performance

subtopics.title: Ticket Server
subtopics.theory:
🔹 D) Ticket Server

Definition

Centralized service that generates incremental IDs.

Flow

Client requests ID

Ticket server increments counter

Returns ID

Advantages

Strict ordering

Simple logic

Disadvantages

Single point of failure

Scalability bottleneck

Network latency added

subtopics.title: Snowflake ID
subtopics.theory:
🔹 E) Snowflake ID (Recommended Solution)



✅ Definition

Snowflake is a distributed 64-bit ID generation algorithm that combines timestamp, machine ID, and sequence number.



✅ 64-bit Structure

Bits

Purpose

1 bit

Sign bit (unused)

41 bits

Timestamp (milliseconds)

10 bits

Machine ID

12 bits

Sequence number



✅ Generation Flow

Get current timestamp

If same millisecond → increment sequence

If sequence limit exceeded → wait next millisecond

Combine:

timestamp

machine ID

sequence

Return 64-bit ID



✅ Important Points

No central coordination

Time sortable

Scales horizontally

O(1) generation

Millions IDs/sec per node



✅ Advantages

Globally unique

Time ordered

Highly scalable

No bottleneck

High availability



❌ Disadvantages

Clock synchronization issues

Machine ID management needed

Slight implementation complexity

subtopics.title: Clock Synchronization Issue
subtopics.theory:
3️⃣ Clock Synchronization Issue

Definition

Occurs when system clock moves backward, risking duplicate or out-of-order IDs.

Solutions

Block until clock catches up

Use logical timestamp

Reject requests temporarily

subtopics.title: Important Terms
subtopics.theory:
5️⃣ Important Terms (Definitions for Interview)

Distributed System

System where components run on multiple networked machines.

Uniqueness

Guarantee that no two IDs are identical.

Sortable

IDs increase over time.

Scalability

Ability to handle increased load by adding machines.

Horizontal Scaling

Adding more servers instead of upgrading one.

Bottleneck

Component that limits system performance.

Single Point of Failure (SPOF)

One component whose failure stops the system.

Epoch

Custom starting time used for timestamp calculation.

Machine ID

Unique identifier assigned to each server.

Sequence Number

Counter to generate multiple IDs in same millisecond.

Monotonicity

Property where values always increase.

subtopics.title: Final Interview One-Liner
subtopics.theory:
🎯 Final Interview One-Liner

Snowflake-style ID generation is the optimal solution because it generates 64-bit, globally unique, time-ordered IDs without centralized coordination.
